geo.title: Get started
geo.body:
Slice clay solids with dental floss.

Goal: I can identify nets and cross sections of solids.

slides.title: The big idea
slides.html:
A net is a flat pattern that folds into a solid. A cube has 11 different nets of six squares.

A cross section is the shape where a plane slices a solid. Slicing a cube can give a triangle, a square, a rectangle, a pentagon or even a regular hexagon (through the midpoints of six edges). A plane perpendicular to a right circular cylinder's axis gives a disk. An oblique, nonaxial plane gives a full elliptical disk only when the intersection is not clipped by either finite end. A plane parallel to the axis through the interior gives a rectangle; tangent/supporting positions can be degenerate. Slicing a cone parallel to its base gives a smaller circle.

Slice a solid with a moving plane and see the cross section.

slides.title: Check yourself
slides.html: Can a cross section of a cube be a regular hexagon?
slides.reveal: Yes, a plane through the midpoints of six edges, perpendicular to a long diagonal.
